note.question: How do policies for managing cash and digital currency inventories interact in the developing world?
note.overview: Mobile money systems—platforms built and managed by mobile network platform operators (MMPOs) to allow money to be stored as digital currency—connect millions of poor and “unbanked” people to the formal financial system. Unfortunately, low service levels because of the suboptimal management of cash and digital currency (e-float) inventory impede the development of these ecosystems. Accordingly, we seek to answer the question of how agents should manage inventories of cash and e-float.

source.section: Formulation of the Agent’s Optimal Inventory
source.quote: Here, we assume that T is large enough (or equivalently, that the time interval t is small enough) such that the probabil­ ity of more than one demand arriving within a period t is sufficiently small.

In this setting, the agent not only serves uncertain demand for cash and e-float, but each sale of cash (e-float) also generates equivalent inventory of e-float (cash; i.e., agents not only face stochastic de­ mand, as is typical in many inventory settings, but they also face symmetric, stochastic replenishment for each good through sales of the other good).
Thus, we equip MMPOs with guidance as to whom to target and how.
